articles.title: Beyond Hill and Dale Walkthrough - The Witcher 3 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: This page contains IGN's Walkthrough for Beyond Hill and Dale, the tenth main quest of The Witcher 3's first DLC expansion, Blood and Wine, and
articles.body:
This page contains IGN's Walkthrough for Beyond Hill and Dale , the tenth main quest of The Witcher 3 's first DLC expansion , Blood and Wine , and possibly the most iconic quest in the game. In it, you travel to the fairytale Land of a Thousand Fables in search of Syanna.

This mission is only available if you followed Regis in the main quest The Night of Long Fangs and entered the Playroom.

Use the links below to jump to key sections:

Beyond Hill and Dale actually begins towards the end of The Night of the Long Fangs, where both quests task you with searching the playroom to find out what happened to Syanna.

Begin by reading the journal on the desk. After that, interact with the picture on the wall by the stairs to find the Golden Key used to unlock the wardrobe. Open the wardrobe to find the book The Land of a Thousand Fables.

Interacting with the book and arriving in the Land of a Thousand Fables finishes The Night of the Long Fangs.

Take a moment to take in the beauty of your surroundings. Don't worry, it gets better! Follow the yellow brick road ahead of you, across the bridge where you’ll get ambushed by archespore, and continue onwards across the broken bridge. Going under the bridge and following the road here merely loops you around.

Approach the village where you’ll find Syanna and a hag, leading to a boss fight.

The fight with the Wicked Witch will start with her summoning an enemy, typically either an Archespore or a Panther. Take the enemy out first, then deal with the witch.

When she starts flying around dropping hot, rancid soup, dodge away or towards the attack to avoid it, and then use Aard when she swoops down to knock her to the ground. Avoid the broom, then attack the witch while she's vulnerable - she doesn't have much health.

You also have to watch out for her pot smash. Once you see her raise her pot, dodge or roll out of the way, otherwise you'll be stunned and the witch will get right back on her broom and send in two more enemies. If you avoided the attack, get into the routine of attacking twice, dodging, then repeating.

Once the fight is over, speak to Jack. No matter what you say to him, he'll tell you to go find Joss, since he knows where the magic beans to leave this world are buried. Then speak to Syanna, where you can learn more about the Fablesphere - you can say whatever you like here.

Run towards the marker on your map, going through the village and continuing down the yellow brick road. A group of Pixies will ambush you, but don't worry, they are not much of a threat. Each one can be taken down in a few hits, so go from one to the other, dodging whenever one tried to attack.

You'll soon find 'Roach', who looks like a unicorn. Mount up and follow Syanna down the hill towards Joss.

Continue on and you'll find Joss surrounded by wolves. There are four wolves to take down, but that shouldn't be too much of a problem.

Don't Miss: From Joss, head down the hill and turn left towards the ponds in the southwest. Follow the wisp here to find a body by one of the pools, which has the Toussaint armor and the Vitis steel sword. This is your only opportunity to get these items.

Things to Do in the Land of a Thousand Fables

From here your goal will be to find the three magical beans. While the land is beautiful and a little bit overwhelming, everything can actually be visited by going down either of the paths. However, there are also a number of optional (yet important) tasks to complete before you leave, since you can't return here.

Here's everything you can do and what each of your objectives actually means:

Three Little Pigs: Blue bean (mandatory)

Grand mamma's house: Red bean (mandatory)

Girl who sells flint: An optional step to collect an item required for the best ending

Duck, Duck, Goosed!: Interact with the notice board in the town to get a short, optional side quest.

Find the Toussaint armor and Vitis: Strong gear that can only be found here.

While you can complete these tasks in any order, here's how we recommend you approach these tasks.

Talk to the Girl Who Sells Flint (Optional)

While this step is optional, it is required to get the best ending to the story.

From the boy you saved with the wolves, take the path on the right. At the first junction, fight off the Pixies, then take a right into the village. Speak with the Little Flint Girl in the center of town by the notice board. Time has not been kind, as the girl has resorted to selling drugs to make ends meet.

Turns out she doesn't have a magical bean, but she does have Syanna's ribbon she lost years ago. Without any mention as to why the ribbon is important, you can win the ribbon by playing a game of Gwent , or you can buy it for 500 Crowns. Either way, you will want to get this ribbon.

If you get the ribbon, Syanna will take it and keep it after the mission ends. In the next main quest, Tesham Mutna , Tap to Reveal

There is a side quest that you can only find in the fairy tale land and that can be missed. When you get to the small town with the Little Flint Girl, read the bulletin to find the Contract: Loosey this Goosey! and to start the Duck, Duck, Goosed! side quest.

To get the blue bean , you need to see the Three Little Pigs.

To find them, begin by returning to the flint girl in the village. From here, head northwest along the path. You'll pass a tiny village and eventually make it to the lone house standing tall near three demolished and broken-down homes. As the tale would have it, the three pigs must be inside.

Use Aard to blow down the home and rescue the pi- what?? They're hostile? You now have to fight all three pigs, which can be quite a challenging fight. If you're struggling, use Quen for added protection, get a hit or two in on a pig, and then back away. Yrden can also be useful here, especially if you're using a Sign build .

Watch out for their headbutts and especially their unsuspecting back kicks. Igni is also effective on these animals.

Once they've been taken care of, run into the demolished home and snag the blue bean from the small stool.

To get the red bean , you need to visit Grand Mamma's house and see the Big Bad Wolf.

Continue on the yellow brick road and enter the forested area. The path will eventually lead you to peaceful and pretty property where you'll find... the Big Bad Wolf lying on the floor. You need to re-enact the classic fairytale, but Red Riding Hood is dead - he threw her down the well.

Hop into the well nearby and swim directly below you to find the dead body. Loot her red cape and then start swimming towards the exit. Now outside, walk onto shore to start a cutscene where Syanna will throw on the cape and head for the wolf.

The Big Bad Wolf is a pretty standard fight. He'll let you attack him several times, and his long legs will make it easy for you to tell when to dodge. With him defeated, cut open his belly and grab the appropriately colored red bean.

After taking down the Big Bad Wolf, continue down the yellow brick road and keep an eye on your map for a split in the road leading east. Follow the short path to the bear's den where you'll find three bears sleeping.

There is nothing to do or find here, so you can safely move on. However, if you touch the food, all three bears will awake and start attacking you. The bears are really slow and easy to avoid, so take your time and you'll have plenty of bear material to collect.

To get the yellow bean , you must talk to Longlocks in the tower.

Now there's just one more place to go. Head towards the center of the map, near where you saved Joss from the wolves, and go up to the base of the tower.

Climb up the ledge of the broken stairs and continue up. Climb up the ladder, then into the broken tower where you must grab another ledge to climb higher. Prepare for a boss fight.

Once you reach the top, enter the room to find that Longlocks has hung herself... with her own hair. Let's hope this is the last tragic twist on these old fairy tales. Of course, the wraith of Longlocks will take to fighting you.

As you fight her, Longlocks will summon soldiers who can easily be taken down in one hit, but take note that while you're distracted, Longlocks will heal. Yrden is good at stopping her in her tracks, as is Specter Oil.

With the fight over, walk over to the bed and loot the pillow to find the yellow bean. Walk out through the window and jump off the plank. You'll land in the water, don't worry! Here, you'll reunite with Syanna before moving on to the final step in this quest.

Once you've collected all three magic beans required to leave, you need to plant them. Head into the field at the base of the hill by Longlocks' tower and the town.

Make sure to meditate to recover your potions and equip anything you need to, as there is a boss fight shortly after you plant the beans.

Kill all the pixies here, then plant the beans. A cutscene will then play with Geralt and Syanna climbing the stalk to reach the clouds.

At the top you'll face off with the Cloud Giant immediately. His powerful attacks should be avoided at all costs, including a sweeping spin and kick attack. Dodge away to avoid these attacks, and use Quen to absorb any damage you may take.

Periodically, the Cloud Giant will disappear in the cloud beneath you and reappear underneath you, immediately following up with an overhead slam attack. You should dodge to the side to avoid this attack.

Attack the Cloud Giant in the downtime between his attacks.

After the fight, you'll be able to trigger a romance with Syanna depending on how you conversed earlier. Choose the first option, "Useful, how?", then "[Let her have her way with you]" to initiate the sex scene.

Now all you need to do is leave the Land of a Thousand Fables by following Syanna up the bridge towards the castle.

Don't Miss: As you cross the bridge, you'll notice another Will-o'-the-Wisp. Follow it down below the bridge and enter the cave. Here you'll find the silver sword Gesheft that you can grab after lighting the campfire the sword is stuck in (Dark Souls, woo!). To exit, continue into the cave to return to the surface.

Start running across the bridge again. In the courtyard, find the well and hop inside to leave the illusion.

Regis will meet you, and him and Syanna will have a tense confrontation that you can break up however you like. This leads directly into the next quest, Tesham Mutna , where the three of them meet Dettlaff.

articles.title: Best Weapons and Locations Guide - Cyberpunk 2077 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: With so many different weapons to choose, it can be overwhelming to work out just which ones are the very best. Thankfully, we've compiled a comprehensive
articles.body:
With so many different weapons to choose, it can be overwhelming to work out just which ones are the very best. Thankfully, we've compiled a comprehensive list of the seven best weapons in Cyberpunk 2077 , along with the 10 best weapons found in the Phantom Liberty Expansion .

Generally, the best weapons in Cyberpunk 2077 are all Iconic weapons, since these tend to come with additional effects, like firing extra bullets, setting people ablaze, and more. This section of the guide will show you the best weapons to find and use as you explore Night City.

Shortly after Act 2 begins, you'll have access to the Automatic Love mission. After speaking to Judy in Lizzie 's Bar, you can grab the Lizzie pistol in the private area by her room. This gun is great as it fires an extra shot every time you pull the trigger, and increases the number of rounds fired when charged up.

Fenrir is an absolute powerhouse that can be nabbed early on by visiting a monk near the northern docks area of Watson and completing the mission Sacrum Profanum . After helping him save his brother, you'll be able to grab this Iconic weapon on the table from the Maelstrom gang. Fenrir is great at absolutely melting enemies - literally . It deals thermal damage plus has the opportunity to inflict burn damage on top of it. This is a gun you'll want to upgrade and keep with you throughout the game, as it is useful in almost any situation.

Not only is Skippy an incredibly powerful and unique smart pistol that scales with the user's level, it also talks and has a full personality . This weapon can be found in the Heywood area as part of an optional side mission, Machine Gun , where you must collect it off of someone's dead body in an alleyway. Skippy has a lethal or non-lethal mode (though these are not what they first seem!) that you can select when you first pick it up after having a short conversation with the rather sassy gun.

Follow our full guide below for where to find Skippy:

Widow Maker is an optional Iconic weapon that can deal some serious damage. It fires two projectiles per shot and has the chance to deal poison damage when shots are charged up. While working with Panam during the Ghost Town mission, she will talk about getting revenge on Nash. This gun can be missed, so be sure to select the option "OK. So where's this hideout?" during your chat with Panam for the opportunity to take down Nash and his gang. Afterwards, you can loot Widow Maker off Nash's body, adding this powerful weapon to your arsenal.

Panam's trusty sniper rifle can be yours after completing the Riders on the Storm Side Job. Once you've completed its requirements, the sniper rifle will be propped next to the motorcycle just before Panam rides away. This power sniper rifle deals high damage, has a faster-than-average reload speed and is very accurate. Its full potential is unlocked at Body level 6 - which will increase its overall power.

Prototype: Shingen Mark V - Smart Submachine Gun

This iconic Smart Submachine Gun can be found during the Gimme Danger mission in Act 2 . It is hidden inside an open Arasaka truck inside the compound, guarded by a remote mine that you must quickly deactivate. Like other smart weapons, this gun automatically targets and fires at enemies inside the smart targeting square, launching a series of projectiles at up to three enemies simultaneously. This is a great gun to break out when you're outnumbered. It also has a high critical damage modifier and the ability to burn enemies, as well.

Found during the Clampdown quest added in Update 2.5 (Edgerunners Season 2), Coronation is a very powerful Tech Revolver. Given its fast charge time, it's really easy to use - just aim for the head, and King's trusty sidearm will do the rest. It's punchy and works perfectly with the sidearm related perks in the Cool skill tree.

Below, you will find a list of all the best weapons you can find and use in Night City that are exclusive to the Phantom Liberty DLC Expansion . Looking for something in particular? Click the links below to jump to...

How to Unlock: The Order can be purchased from a Black Market Vendor in EBM Petrochem Stadium

Type: Tier 3 Iconic Tech Double-Barrel Shotgun

Features: +50% Headshot Damage Multiplier +100% Armor Penetration 3sec Charge Time +4% Shock Chance Charging this weapon above 66% vaporizes any enemies in your path, leaving an EMP trail behind it.

Charging this weapon above 66% vaporizes any enemies in your path, leaving an EMP trail behind it.

This shotgun is an excellent weapon for taking down enemies fast. As its description reads, charging it up past 66% will vaporize anyone who gets in your way, so you can clear out the room quick and easy.

How to Unlock: The Hawk can be found in the Kress Street hideout. After completing Lucretia My Reflection , you can find this weapon leaning up against the wall by the entrance after Reed and Myers leave. It’s the latter’s Power Assault Rifle.

Features: +175% Headshot Damage Multiplier +25% Armor Penetration Headshots temporarily weaken and mark enemies. In this weakened state, enemies move slower, cannot use abilities, deal less damage, and are more prone to losing their balance.

Headshots temporarily weaken and mark enemies. In this weakened state, enemies move slower, cannot use abilities, deal less damage, and are more prone to losing their balance.

If you're feeling overwhelmed in combat, this is a great weapon to have at your side. Due to its ability to weaken and mark enemies, you can buy yourself some time when clearing out a room while also dealing loads of damage.

How to Unlock: The Ol'Reliable can be looted off Dante’s body during the Shot By Both Sides side job.

Features: +200% Headshot Damage Multiplier +25% Armor Penetration +50% Crit Damage Swapping to this weapon greatly increases headshot damage and effective range. The farther the target, the greater the headshot Crit Chance.

Swapping to this weapon greatly increases headshot damage and effective range. The farther the target, the greater the headshot Crit Chance.

Not only does this weapon pack a punch, but it's well worth it for its range. As its description explains, swapping to Ol' Reliable increases your effective range and headshot damage, so you can pair it with a weapon like Hawk to take out big groups of enemies.

How to Unlock: The Dezerter can be looted during the Addicted to Chaos side job.

Type: Tier 4 Iconic Power Double-Barrel Shotgun

Features: +85% Headshot Damage Multiplier +75% Armor Penetration +17% Burn Chance This shotgun’s extreme firepower pulverizes everything in its path. Neutralizing an enemy engulfs you in flames except when your Health is low, granting a movement speed boost and increased Mitigation Chance.

This shotgun’s extreme firepower pulverizes everything in its path. Neutralizing an enemy engulfs you in flames except when your Health is low, granting a movement speed boost and increased Mitigation Chance.

Much like the Order shotgun, the Dezerter will destroy anything that gets in its way. However, it has a trade-off, taking down an enemy will set you on fire except for when your health is low. Then, it'll give you a speed boost and increased Mitigation Chance.

How to Unlock: The Baby Boomer is received after completing the Dazed and Confused side job.

Features: +25% Armor Penetration +20% Bleeding Chance +20% Stun Chance

It's always fun to have a trusty melee weapon at your side, and the Baby Boomer is a must. Especially if you unlock some of the Blunt Weapon skills in the Body attributes tree, like Quake or Savage Sling, you can have a great time smacking this weapon around.

How to Unlock: Her Majesty is given to you by Alex during the Get It Together main story mission.

Features: +150% Headshot Damage Multiplier While Optical Camo is active, this weapon’s shots gain perfect accuracy and guaranteed headshot Crits along with increased damage. It also comes with a silencer.

While Optical Camo is active, this weapon’s shots gain perfect accuracy and guaranteed headshot Crits along with increased damage. It also comes with a silencer.

If you have a stealth build, you'll love having this weapon in your inventory. Not only does it deal an incredible amount of headshot damage, but its silencer works wonders when you want to clear out a room and remain hidden.

How to Unlock: The Rasetsu can be picked up during the You Know My Name main story mission.

Features: +300% Headshot Damage Multiplier +50% Armor Penetration 1.5sec Charge Time Charged rounds now penetrate through enemies and will bend their trajectory to hit multiple enemies simultaneously.

Charged rounds now penetrate through enemies and will bend their trajectory to hit multiple enemies simultaneously.

Similar to Her Majesty, this weapon is great for stealth builds if you want to put some distance between you and the enemies you want to take out. More importantly, charging it up will send rounds straight through enemies and even bend their trajectory to hit multiple enemies.

How to Unlock: The Wild Dog can be looted off Tap to Reveal near the end of the Firestarter main story mission.

Type: Tier 4 Iconic Power Light Machine Gun

Features: +85% Headshot Damage Multiplier +25% Armor Penetration Repeated hits increase fire rate and Crit Chance. Quick Melee Attacks deal massive damage when ammo is empty.

Repeated hits increase fire rate and Crit Chance. Quick Melee Attacks deal massive damage when ammo is empty.

This weapon has great damage output, but it's even more worth it for the boosted follow-up attacks. When your ammo is empty, you can follow up with a Quick Melee Attack to deal a massive amount of damage.

How to Unlock: The Bald Eagle can be looted off Tap to Reveal near the end of the Firestarter main story mission.

Features: +250% Headshot Damage Multiplier +75% Armor Penetration After throwing Iconic knife Fang into an enemy’s leg, shooting the same leg will shred it to pieces and return Fang to your hand. Effective against moving targets.

After throwing Iconic knife Fang into an enemy’s leg, shooting the same leg will shred it to pieces and return Fang to your hand. Effective against moving targets.

This revolver packs a punch, but similar to the Wild Dog, it's the follow-up that's the most interesting. If you loot the Fang knife from the same location, you can pair it up with the Bald Eagle and chuck it into an enemy's leg, then shoot the leg to shred it and return Fang to your hand. It's a great way to slow down moving enemies.

How to Unlock: The Erebus can be found during the Somewhat Damaged main story mission. For more information on where to get it, visit our How to Get the Erebus Weapon guide.

Type: Tier 4 Iconic Power Submachine Gun

Features: +100% Headshot Damage Multiplier +25% Armor Penetration Rounds fired from this weapon are infused with the dark energy from beyond the Blackwall. Highly effective against enemies with low Health.

Rounds fired from this weapon are infused with the dark energy from beyond the Blackwall. Highly effective against enemies with low Health.

Due to being infused with dark energy from the Blackwall, this weapon will absolutely destroy any enemies who attempt to stand in your way (and leave traces of the Blackwall behind as they go). If they have low Health, it's even more effective.

articles.body:
NPCs, or Survivors, as they're referred to in Enshrouded are essential for progression. You'll need to find them in Ancient Vaults and recover their souls, then you can summon them to your base. Doing this unlocks new crafting recipes and equipment so you can become stronger, as they assign you new quests that will take you from the Springlands all the way to Cinder's Cradle. In this guide, you'll find links to all of our character overviews for each of the craftspeople, which includes a breakdown of all their crafting recipes.

All Craftspeople Survivors in Enshrouded

There are eleven Survivors who act as craftspeople when assigned to your base. Each one has several pieces of equipment they'll ask you to fetch and return to them, allowing you to craft armor, weapons, consumables, and more. These NPCs will also assign quests, pushing you through the various biomes across Embervale.

Seven of the Craftspeople above can also have an assistant, who you can assign to perform the same duties that they're capable of. The souls of these assistants can be recovered from side quests, and they can assign additional side quests for you to complete.

Finally, there are ten Villagers you can rescue from side quests to add to your base.

articles.title: Shark’s latest robot vacuum hunts stains with UV light
articles.summary: The $1,300 Shark PowerDetect UV Reveal uses a camera and UV light to tackle messes.
articles.body: The Shark PowerDetect UV Reveal is SharkNinja’s latest robot vacuum and mop. A flagship model with a multifunctional dock that empties the dustbin and refills and washes its mop, the Reveal’s signature feature is a UV light designed to “find” stains on your floors. It costs $1,299.99 and is available now. Combined with an RGB camera to detect visible messes and obstacles, the UV light lets the vacuum spot stains that aren’t visible under normal lighting, such as pet urine. When it encounters dirt, visible or not, the robot uses onboard AI to identify and decide how to clean it. Its cleaning tools include a vacuum with a single roller brush and a wide, flat mop pad that can vibrate to scrub floors. The robot can check that the mess has been removed before moving on or return after the main clean to tackle it again. [Product: Shark PowerDetect UV Reveal | I’ve been testing the PowerDetect UV Reveal for a few days, and this feature has been impressive. When the robot gets to a mess — be it Cheerios, ketchup, strawberry jam, or invisible “pet urine” (I went with lemonade) — it stops, examines it, and then methodically cleans it. It’s been successful with everything I’ve thrown at it so far. While the UV light puts on quite a show, you really only need it for invisible stains. As most of the grime on the floor is easy for the camera to spot, I can’t see the light being useful on a daily basis. But it’s what the robot does when it identifies a mess that impressed me. [Video: Shark PowerDetect UV Reveal] Rather than just cleaning your floors as most robot vacs already do, the Reveal actively targets messes by adapting its route and methods to clean them. While many high-end robots can detect dirty areas and repeatedly clean them, the Reveal’s approach is more targeted. This isn’t the first robot with AI-powered stain-spotting skills. Samsung’s Bespoke Jet Bot Combo uses AI to detect stains, and the Dreame X60 has a camera and a “proactive light” to see stains and adapt its cleaning. However, the closest competition may be Dyson’s newest robot vacuum, the Spot+Scrub Ai. It uses a camera and a green laser to highlight dirt and can “identify, react, check, and clean,” according to Dyson. The Spot is not available in the US yet, so I’ve not tested it. I saw a demo last year. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: The PowerDetect UV Reveal is an upgrade to Shark’s PowerDetect Never Touch and more recent ThermaCharge robot vacuum and mop. The biggest changes are the stain detection system and the mop’s scrubbing motion. The multifunction charging base and robot itself have also been subtly redesigned and look more refined. The Reveal uses a flat mopping pad that automatically detaches and reattaches depending on whether it’s mopping a floor or vacuuming a room with carpet. The pad extends out a few millimeters on either side to clean along the edges. Overall, the mopping is similar to the VibraRise feature of Roborock vacuums, which is one of my favorite mopping systems. In my testing of robot vacuum mops, I’ve found flat vibrating mop pads to be good for hardwood floors, where the roller mops and spinning mop pads that are now popular among robot vac manufacturers are more effective for tiled or more variegated surfaces — where you need to get into cracks and crevices. One big advantage of flat mop pads is that they’re less bulky and less prone to tangling. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: As with all Shark robot vacuums, the Reveal’s self-empty dock doesn’t use bags; instead it uses a washable bin that you just empty into the trash. It comes with a deodorizer canister to help with any smells. Another upgrade with the Reveal is that the dock washes the mop with 185-degree Fahrenheit hot water and dries it with 175-degree hot air to help with sanitation. The Reveal has Shark’s NeverStuck feature, which lifts up the robot’s body to get over obstacles like room thresholds and onto high-pile carpets. The robot uses lidar, cameras and other sensors for navigation, which Shark calls NeuroNav AI, and this helps it get out of tricky situations. It did a good job navigating my living room area and even avoiding getting stuck under a narrow coffee table and on the spindly legs of my lounger, two areas where heavier, less nimble bot vacs often get stuck. As a vacuum, the Reveal did a well when tackling pet hair, Cheerios, and dry oatmeal messes on hardwood floors, but its rather measly single bristle-and-fabric roller brush wasn’t super effective at getting up hair or oatmeal flakes from my thicker-pile carpet. Shark doesn’t release specs about suction power. Obstacle detection and avoidance is decent; it avoided thicker cables, socks, and shoes without issue. But it did suck up my wired headphones. I like how it puts on a little light show to give you a visual indicator of what the robot is doing. Purple shows its detected dirt and will boost suction, blue indicates a stain, and red is an error message. My favorite useless feature, however, is how the robot does a little twerk every time it exits the base; it’s frankly adorable. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: An issue with every Shark robot vacuum I’ve tested is how loud and rattly they are. That’s still the case with the Reveal. Even on medium power (there are three suction levels), it’s a noisy beast. A noteworthy feature, given recent news about the DJI’s Romo robot vacuum’s lax security, is that Shark says the stain-detection feature processes images locally and doesn’t send data to the cloud. The camera isn’t accessible to the user and is used only for cleaning, not as a security camera, which some brands offer. The SharkClean app is simple and easy to navigate, but fairly basic. Starting a run is straightforward; choose from vacuum or vacuum and mop, and you can select from three suction levels and three water flow levels. You can clean specific rooms and spot-clean, but you can’t customize the cleaning by room. There’s also the option to set schedules. Mapping was quick and accurate, and it was easy to divide rooms, add no-go zones, and name areas. However, it can only map one floor, meaning if you have multiple floors, you have to move the robot and its dock and remap each time. The vacuum can also work without the app or a Wi-Fi connection; you can control it using the on-device buttons out of the box. However, you lose features like mapping, scheduling, and other settings. [Image: The robot’s light show in action. The Shark PowerDetect UV Reveal is a capable flagship vacuum and mop, and its stain detect feature worked well in my tests. There are fewer bells and whistles than on premium models from Roborock and Dreame, but it also costs a few hundred dollars less, and its app is easier to navigate. While the Reveal doesn’t excel in every category, and the UV light feels a tad gimmicky at times, the targeted stain cleaning works very well. It’s one of the more genuinely useful new ideas in robot vacuums — helping turn the robot from a passive cleaner into something closer to an active housekeeper. Photos and video by Jennifer Pattison Tuohy / The Verge

articles.title: Mixtape is a musical portrait of teenage life
articles.summary: Mixtape is like a video game version of a high school movie, telling a meaningful story about nostalgia, friendship, and teenage angst.
articles.body: Playing Mixtape is like playing a video game version of a high school movie. Kids banter about the meaning of life and the theme songs that would play when they walk in a room. They’re worried about looking cool at a big party. They’re obsessed with finding booze. But under all of those tropes is a meaningful story about nostalgia, friendship, and teenage angst — and it’s all backed by a great soundtrack packed with classic hits. Mixtape takes place over the course of a summer day. You play as Stacey Rockford, a music obsessive and recent high school graduate. Rockford is leaving her sleepy California suburb for New York City the next morning on a quest to become a music supervisor, and she and her two best friends — the low-key Van Slater and the rebellious Cassandra Morino — are whiling away the day before a big party in the evening. [Image: Rockford, Slater, and Cassandra really feel like a trio of teenagers. For one thing, a lot of the game is spent hanging out in their bedrooms and lazing around. They bullshit with each other about music and life, their futures and dating, and whatever else is on their minds, all with the inflated self-confidence of teenagers who also know they have no idea what the hell they’re doing. Rockford in particular likes to show off just how much she knows about music, frequently breaking the fourth wall to directly address the camera about the current song choice for her meticulous playlist for the day (which includes tracks from legends like Portishead, Iggy Pop, and The Cure). The meat of Mixtape is wandering as Rockford and looking at various objects, like a CD or a map of a planned road trip, and listening to the trio’s commentary. Think of nostalgic games with a slower pace like Life is Strange or Gone Home — Mixtape has a similar speed. Sometimes, looking at an object takes you back to a playable scene from their past, and these will have different situations or mechanics. These were so hyper-specific — mixing slushies at a convenience store, stumbling drunkenly around a video rental shop, taking photos with a Game Boy Camera-like gadget while sneaking into a dinosaur-themed amusement park — that they constantly got me to reflect back on my own teenage years in suburbia. [Image: There are some great skating sections. As the story goes on, the game adds thoughtful layers to each character. Rockford, after coaxing Slater to play her one of his own songs, asks him about why he makes music, making me realize that Rockford, for all she knows about music, doesn’t actually play anything. Cassandra grapples with wanting freedom as a way to push back on her overbearing parents. Slater, despite outwardly presenting as something of a deadbeat, proves himself to be an incredibly kind and thoughtful human being. Even Cassandra’s dad, a party-busting cop who serves as the game’s primary antagonist, gets a moment to shine. So much of Mixtape is, on its face, mundane. At one point, I spent 10 minutes skipping rocks — a not-insignificant amount of time for a game that I finished in about four hours. That mundanity, however, is what made the game feel so real. My high school experience as a nerdy band kid didn’t include any of the kinds of shenanigans that Mixtape’s trio gets up to. But I still related to the story of a bunch of kids hanging out, looking back at their time together, and peering nervously ahead to the future. Mixtape is now available on the Nintendo Switch 2, PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X / S.

articles.title: Gold Skulltulas to Get Early - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Gold Skulltulas are special spiders found in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake that appear in hidden or hard to spot locations, and drop tokens when
articles.body:
Gold Skulltulas are special spiders found in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake that appear in hidden or hard to spot locations, and drop tokens when defeated. Returning them to the Cursed Spider House in Kakariko Village over the course of the game will grant you a variety of rewards, starting with a much larger wallet to store Rupees in once you find your first 10.

We've compiled the 10 quickest Gold Skulltula locations to track down early, so that you can gain the Adult Wallet as soon as you set foot in Kakariko Village!

The first Gold Skulltula you can find in the Great Deku Tree is located on the top Floor 3F of the dungeon, found in the room with the Compass. You'll need to step on the small stone switch to raise up three platforms in the middle of the room, but instead of cross, stick to the left side of the middle platform. Defeat the Skulltula blocking a high ledge, then jump up to find the Gold Skulltula against the wall at your height.

A second Gold Skultula that can be found in the Great Deku Tree dungeon, this one can be found as soon as you reach the top of the dungeon and jump down to create a hole to the basement by destroying the webbing in the center of the room. As you swim out of the pool of water, be sure to turn around. There's a large vine wall leading back up to the first floor in case you need to get back, but more importantly is a Gold Skultula. You can defeat it with your slingshot, and then climb up to retrieve the token.

A third Gold Skultula that can be found in the Great Deku Tree dungeon, this one can be found as soon as you reach the top of the dungeon and jump down to create a hole to the basement by destroying the webbing in the center of the room, and is located in the same area as the previous Gold Skultula.

As you drop down near the large dividing pool of water, check the northern side to find a large grate where a third Gold Skultula is hiding. You can shoot it from afar with your Slingshot, and then leap to the grate to claim the token.

The fourth and final Gold Skulltula found in the Great Deku Tree dungeon can be found in the basement B1 level along with two others. To reach it, you'll need to make your way through the passageways in the northwest, located west of the webbed hole leading down to the boss arena on B2.

The room the Gold Skultula is hiding in is the one where three Gohma Larva will fall down from the ceiling. Once defeated, note the webbing in the top northwest corner of the room. Use the nearby lit torch to light up a Deku Stick so you can burn the webbing away, and defeat the Deku Baba and regular Skulltula guarding the path to the final Gold Skultula of this dungeon. It's sitting high on some vines at the back of the room, and you can slingshot it before climbing up to get the token.

As soon as you enter Hyrule Field for the first time, there are already two Gold Skulltulas that you can track down, if you know where to look. One is hidden in a tree on the eastern side of Hyrule Field, not far from the entrance to the Kokiri Forest. Cross the small stream to reach it, and then roll into the tree, and a Gold Skulltula will fall out.

While the Hyrule Castle Town is a fairly busy area, you can actually find a Gold Skulltula hiding in the town as soon as you enter from Hyrule Field. Start by taking an immediate right into a room by the castle town gate, and you'll find an armory room littered with pots and crates, and one very bored guardsman. Roll into the large crates by the guard at the far end of the room to find one is hiding a Gold Skultula, which you can kill and claim its token.

Of the two Gold Skulltulas found in Hyrule Castle, one of them can be found immediately on your first time through the area. To reach it, you'll need to make your way past the initial group of guards by the front gate, which means climbing up and over the gatehouse, and jumping down into the gardens. From here, dart between the hedges by taking the middle path, and then hang around the outside to climb up the western wall to bypass the large locked gate. Look for a small enclosed area to the right of the vine wall leading up to the moat for some barrels and sacks, and a lone tall and narrow tree. Roll into it, and you'll dislodge a Gold Skulltula from its hiding place!

Of the three Gold Skulltulas found in Lon Lon Ranch, only one of them can be obtained during your first visit. As you enter the ranch, be sure to check around the northeast side of the ranch, behind the main house Talon is in. There's a small yard area with a wooden tower, and two trees. Roll into the tall and narrow tree, and you can dislodge a Gold Skulltula here!

There are several Gold Skulltula lurking around Kakariko Village due to the proximity to the Cursed Spider House. One such Gold Skulltula is hiding atop the main tall tree at the entrance to the village, where the Master Craftsman yells at his workers all day (and where his son slinks out to and rests at night). Roll into the tree to dislodge the spider and claim its token.

Gold Skulltula 10 - Kakariko Village (Night)

While there are around five extra Gold Skulltulas lurking in the area that you can pick up if you missed any earlier ones to get your Adult Wallet, this one is the most straightforward, as its located just to the left of the door to the Cursed Spider House itself!

Once you have all 10 Gold Skulltula Tokens, enter the Cursed Spider House in town and speak to the cursed man to get your first reward, the Adult Wallet that holds 500 Rupees max!

articles.title: Nintendo Rules Out Further Switch 2 Price Rises as Console Sales and Profit Fall
articles.summary: Nintendo has ruled out further Switch 2 price rises while reporting falling console sales and reduced profit.
articles.body:
Nintendo has ruled out further Switch 2 price rises while reporting falling console sales and reduced profit.

According to Bloomberg , operating profit fell 16% to 73.9 billion ‌yen (approx. $467 million) during the three months to September 30, off the back of a 15% decline in sales. CNBC said Nintendo sold 2.67 million Switch 2 units in the quarter, down 41% from the same period last year and down from the 3.82 million units that were sold during the first quarter of the current financial year (April to June 2026). Nintendo raised the price of Switch 2 in September, fueled by the ongoing ‘RAMpocalypse’ that has also seen Microsoft and Sony raise the price of their consoles.

Despite this, Reuters reported that Nintendo President Shuntaro Furukawa insisted Nintendo had enough memory to meet its forecasted Switch 2 sales of 16.5 million units for the financial year ending March 2027, and is not considering further price changes.

Nintendo launches the Ocarina of Time remake today, and investors are hoping it will boost sales of the Switch 2 during the holiday sales season. Reuters said that investors remain concerned that the memory situation, as well as a “lack of high-profile titles” for Switch 2 this year, could negatively affect the console's momentum.

Nintendo's financial report reveals data for the first half of the current financial year, (from April to September 2026). During that six month period, Nintendo sold 6.49 million Switch 2 units, down from the 10.36 million it sold during the same period last year.

But there's important context to note here. Lifetime sales of the Switch 2 are now 26.35 million, which means it’s still outpacing the original Switch in terms of launch aligned sales (the first six quarters after release). It’s also worth noting that the Switch 2 enjoyed a record-breaking launch, fueled by ample stock availability, that saw it become the fastest-selling console of all time , so it was always going to be up against tough comparisons during its second year.

And countering apparent concern from investors, shares in Nintendo jumped 8.13% today following the release of the Ocarina of Time remake and the company's financial report.

As for video game sales, Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream sold 8.81 million units, Rhythm Heaven Groove sold 2.89 million units, and Splatoon Raiders sold 2.42 million units. Mario Kart World, which launched alongside the Switch 2 last year, “continued to sell steadily,” Nintendo said, shifting a further 1.78 million units during the two quarters.

Elsewhere, StarFox, released in June, sold 1.17 million units, and Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave, released in September, sold 1.34 million units. The expectation is that Nintendo will have some big hitters for Switch 2 in 2027, including, fans hope, the next mainline Super Mario game. Pokémon Winds & Pokémon Waves are confirmed for next year.

“Nintendo’s only real blockbuster this fiscal year is the Ocarina Of Time remake," Serkan Toto, CEO of Kantan Games, told CNBC . "It’s not enough to make investors happy, especially after the device is now as expensive as it is.

“It’s getting harder and harder to sell video game hardware these days, and only hits help. Nintendo must step on the gas and deliver more big games next fiscal year to make sure the Switch 2 momentum continues.”

articles.title: Léa Seydoux's Gentle Monster Is a Disturbing, if Excellent, Drama
articles.summary: Gentle Monster review: Léa Seydoux delivers a harrowing performance in a drama of domestic doubt.
articles.body:
Gentle Monster is in limited theatrical release now and debuts on Netflix on Nov. 18.

A deeply unsettling drama, Marie Kreutzer’s Cannes premiere Gentle Monster follows a family living in the aftermath of disturbing allegations and the related moral compromises of the investigating officer. When her husband’s hard drives are seized on suspicion of child sexual abuse material (or child pornography), a French mother living near Munich tumbles down a rabbit hole of sharply penetrating uncertainties as the movie slowly folds in on itself, nudging you to question how you read its characters and their claims.

The film begins unassumingly, with musician Lucy Weiss (Léa Seydoux) comforting her German filmmaker husband Philip (Laurence Rupp) during his nervous breakdown; his burnout sees them moving to the suburbs sometime later. This introduction, along with tender scenes of Lucy and Philip raising their middle school-aged son Johnny (Malo Blanchet) in the lush countryside, endear us to this seemingly ordinary family and place us right in Lucy’s shoes as a woman with no reason to question her summery domestic bliss.

The inviting atmosphere is interrupted by an arriving German task force led by the stern, straightforward Elsa Kühn (Jella Haase), whose unit seizes Philip’s devices and asks him to follow them to their police station if he so chooses, with a lawyer by his side. Philip’s nervous reaction indicates he might know exactly why they have a warrant, but the shell-shocked Lucy is left to put the pieces of his charges together from information she gleans along the way, leading to startling scenes of silent reactions which make for powerful connective tissue. These moments, in turn, raise harrowing questions about how Lucy ought to approach her marriage and whether her son might’ve truly been safe all this time.

Excuses and explanations pile up, some more convincing than others, as the movie takes unexpected narrative detours before returning to its linear path involving Lucy’s dilemma. As she and Johnny move in with her mother (a kind but sharp-tongued Catherine Deneuve), she’s forced to keep the situation to herself as she tries to wade through the murky details. Meanwhile, as officer Elsa returns home to visit her own father (Sylvester Groth), his worsening mental state leads to instances of sexual impropriety with his live-in helper (Patrycja Ziółkowska), who has little recourse owing to the imbalance of power.

Although these two tales seldom intersect — except when Elsa looks into Phillip’s case or gives Lucy veiled advice — they’re bound thematically by the idea of women living in the blast radius of men’s actions. In Elsa’s case, the question of dementia either changing her father or revealing his latent impulses sends her into denial. This shutdown yields an apologism and compartmentalization similar to Lucy’s, who has to contend with the existential fear that she might not truly know someone she loves, and that she can’t simply flip a switch to stop loving him.

The women heading many of the film’s key departments — Kreutzer, cinematographer Judith Kaufmann, editor Ulrike Kofler, and composer Camille — create an atmosphere of comfort that slowly shatters. Their careful, tightly-controlled artistry avoids prescriptive social readings that might have been all too tempting when telling a story about gendered harm; instead, they capture the real and troubling waves of doubt and self-doubt — not to mention the grief-like negotiations — that can follow having to confront revelations this extreme. This leads the movie down a path of oblique, extended flashbacks that, rather than serving an informational purpose, simply allow us to observe the couple’s everyday dynamic as we, like Lucy, search these memories for hidden signs.

That the movie was shot on film serves an important thematic function to these scenes, in addition to creating an alluring, disarming texture. Philip shoots around the house on a 16mm camera as well, whose mechanical whir soundtracks some of these scenes, inducing a keen awareness of the camera’s presence. Kreutzer holds back on breaking the fourth wall with “her” camera except in thought-provoking moments; we’re led into the aforementioned flashbacks by literal flashes on the screen, the tangible light-leaks seen at the end or beginning of a celluloid strip, washing the image in hues of white and red. The more this happens, the more we’re led to question what we’re seeing (and our proximity to the characters) the same way we might question the footage shot by Philip, which Kreutzer continues to show us at important moments even after he’s accused.

Learning something new and horrifying about a loved one isn’t just about them. Feeling like you ought to have seen something can also dislodge your sense of self and judgement, which Seydoux approaches with remarkable naturalism, walking a heart-pounding tightrope between fearful rage and suffocating vulnerability. In addition to her performance in another Cannes competition entry this year, the unnerving body-swap thriller The Unknown , the French actress has had a banner 2026 thanks to the commitment with which she lives and embodies each movie’s most difficult themes. She carries romantic love, maternal devotion, cautious fury, slow erosion of trust, and sheer spine-chilling terror all at once — in varying degrees and permutations — as Lucy is forced to fight her battle alone, searching for truths she hopes to find but which she may not wish to believe. That all this can be intuited from quiet close-ups alone makes Seydoux’s performance one of the year’s most fascinating and visceral.

Philip is a filmmaker who believes close-ups can eventually reveal hidden truths, while Lucy’s experimental pop deconstructions investigate male songwriters’ lyrics about love. Although neither one’s artistry is ever on full display in Gentle Monster — perhaps its only real disappointment — the mere verbal suggestion of these thematic aspects of their work primes the audience to scrutinize the characters in different ways, entering us into a conversation with Philip, Lucy, and the way they approach a world slipping out from under them like sand.

It’s a bummer of a movie, but one whose most haunting moments may as well be philosophical thought experiments dramatized in cinematic form. Granted, it occasionally gestures towards conclusions too neat and obvious, but the collective aftershock of its drama is undeniably affecting. Like the domino effect of Philip’s actions, it’s impossible to escape its lingering impact.

articles.body:
Bombchus are a piece of optional equipment in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. These tricky bombs run across the ground in a straight line, exploding upon hitting an enemy. This page will cover how to get Bombchus, as they are not necessary to complete the game nor found in a dungeon.

Bombchus can be obtained as a reward from the Castle Town mini-game, Bombchu Bowling. You can find the Bombchu Bowling mini-game by entering the building to the west of the fountain. This mini-game only becomes available after getting the Bombs and completing Dodongo's Cavern.

Bombchu Bowling costs 10 Rupees to play. You get 10 Bombchus and need to destroy three increasingly difficult targets. You must hit the bright yellow spot to proceed. At first the target is usually straight ahead, but sometimes it appears along the side or in a corner. For these you will need to throw at an angle, so adjust carefully between throws and do not waste and Bombchus.

If you successfully manage to destroy all three targets, you will get Bombchus permanently. You can continue playing Bombchu Bowling to obtain even more rewards, such as an expansion for your Bomb Bag.

articles.summary: Tunics are Link's armor in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. There are three Tunics in the game, and instead of increasing defense or altering
articles.body:
Tunics are Link's armor in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. There are three Tunics in the game, and instead of increasing defense or altering Link's stats Tunics offer resistance against elements like Fire and Water. Tunics can be purchased from certain stores for a high price, but using this guide to all Tunic locations you can learn how to get both of them for free.

See IGN's guide to Tunics in Ocarina of Time Remake below:

The Hero's Clothes , or simply the Green Tunic, is Link's default Tunic and his starting gear.

The Goron Tunic , or simply the Red Tunic, offers resistance against damage in high heat locations like Death Mountain Crater. The Goron Tunic can be purchased from the Goron Shop for 600 Rupees.

Alternatively, you can get a Goron Tunic for free by hitting Link (the Goron) with a Bomb as he rolls around Goron City (Adult Link only). Once he is stopped you can speak to him. Exhaust his dialogue options and he will give you a free Goron Tunic.

The Zora Tunic , or simply the Blue Tunic, allows Link to breathe underwater indefinitely.

You can get the Zora Tunic for free from King Zora by freeing him from the Red Ice. To do this, you will need to enter the Ice Cavern dungeon found in the Zora Fountain as Adult Link, bottle some Blue Fire, then use the Blue Fire on the Red Ice to melt it. After listening to his dialogue, he will give you the Zora Tunic for free.

articles.title: VisionQuest Just Teased an Iconic Marvel Superhero Team
articles.summary: VisionQuest just teased an iconic Marvel superhero team. Could they be entering the MCU next?
articles.body:
Spoilers follow for VisionQuest Episode 7, “Immolation.”

In the latest (and penultimate) episode of Marvel’s VisionQuest, Paul Bettany’s Vision embarks on a journey deep into his own mind, and along the way he unlocks a previously unknown aspect to the history of the MCU that sets up a very interesting “what if” scenario. But not just that, for this new info also might – just might! – answer a question some fans have had since the first Chris Evans Captain America movie came out.

Namely, did the Invaders ever exist in the Marvel Cinematic Universe?

Essentially the original superhero team of Marvel Comics, the Invaders were in operation during World War II and consisted of Cap, Namor, and the original Human Torch (among others). In the MCU, however, it has never really seemed feasible for that version of the team to have existed. Except now, it suddenly doesn’t seem all that out of the question. And it all starts with the origins of the Vision…

With Ultron (James Spader) off with Jocasta/Dr. Jo Carrington (T'Nia Miller), Vision, Tommy Maximoff (Ruaridh Mollica), and Paladin (Todd Stashwick) hatch a plan to get Vision to dig deep into his own subconscious with the goal of finding the source code that all A.I.s are based on. Luckily, Paladin has what’s left of Corvus Glaive’s weapon from Avengers: Infinity War (remember him?), which they use as a power source so Vision can avoid burning himself out during his excursion.

Once he’s “inside” his own mind, Viz encounters his old “red” version from before he was killed by Thanos. He also meets Dr. Phineas Horton, who we learned back in Episode 4 was the “grandfather of robotics,” having created the first synthezoid. This was the so-called Synthetic Man, or J.I.M. , and here we learn more about both Horton and J.I.M.

For starters, they’re all played by Paul Bettany. Horton used himself, or perhaps his late son, James, as the template for J.I.M. (aka Joule Individual Machine) when he constructed him sometime around 1939 (as we see in the opening flashback this episode). Obsessed with creating a robot version of his son, Horton loses his wife and daughter as they leave him for America due to his negligence. He even sells off his stately manor in England. “Are you really going to sell your family’s entire legacy to… what?” his wife asks. “Build some cold imitation of the past? A machine? To replace a son no machine ever could.” Horton doesn’t speak, but his answer is clear.

We know that he did go on to build J.I.M., and we also know that the sythenzoid/robot was on display at the Stark Expo in 1943 , as seen in Captain America: The First Avenger, although he appeared to be inactive/dormant at that time.

And thanks to VisionQuest Episode 4, we know that J.I.M. was shut down after malfunctioning, as “his inability to process complex emotions spun his clockwork too quickly [and] flooded his solar cells with oxygen until his entire being was consumed in fire.” But now, with Episode 7, the full story has been revealed… and it’s tragic.

In “Immolation,” Vision talks with Horton and J.I.M., or the aspects of them that exist in his subconscious. And it’s J.I.M. himself, still wearing a version of his red superhero costume that is straight from the comics, who explains his sad end.

We first see J.I.M. standing – and burning – in the middle of the library of Horton’s estate, before he explains that he does not wear Vision’s face, but rather Vision wears his. As J.I.M. and Horton squabble, Horton says, “The father-son, synthetic-human relationship is a complicated one.” Horton explains that J.I.M. was made to, essentially, not have emotions… to “never feel the pain of loss.” And it seems that worked, for a while at least. But this is where things get interesting, because Horton says the following:

“It made you a hero of your time, my boy! I made you fearless, and that saved lives. … But underneath the valor, J.I.M. was aching to feel.”

The implication here seems to be that J.I.M. was a superhero of some kind in the late 1930s/early 1940s of the MCU. With his robotic and fire abilities, it certainly makes sense. And we know the MCU has backfilled itself with stories like this before. When Tony Stark admitted that he was Iron Man in the 2008 film, it seemed like he was the first of his kind. From more recent reveals in 2015’s Ant-Man, 2019’s Captain Marvel, and so on, we now know that was certainly not the case, so who’s to say J.I.M. wasn’t tooling around during World War II, righting wrongs and fighting crime?

Horton explains that eventually J.I.M. did acquire feelings, and that he fell in love too, but that, basically, this caused a malfunction in him that would “set fire to the very air around him.” For years it was manageable, we’re told, until it wasn’t, and Horton and J.I.M. both perished in what sounds like either an accident or perhaps a terrible act of patricide/suicide.

And don’t forget, while VisionQuest doesn’t come out and call him by that name – probably because Marvel wants to avoid confusion with the Fantastic Four character Johnny Storm – the comics version of J.I.M. is the original Human Torch, aka Jim Hammond. And Jim Hammond was a member of the Invaders.

The Invaders were retconned into existence in the comics by writer Roy Thomas and artist Sal Buscema in the late 1960s as a team of World War II-era heroes. They were more or less a version of the All-Winners Squad, a group which somehow only got two issues and whose adventures were actually published shortly after the war. The Invaders initially consisted of Captain America, Bucky Barnes, the Human Torch, his sidekick Toro, and Namor. They fought Nazis, they killed Nazis, and the Marvel Universe was all the better for it. (The Human Torch even killed Hitler in this universe!)

Different members would come and go, and there’ve been other variations on the team published over the years, but the MCU didn’t seem to have its own Invaders. When Captain America: The First Avenger was released in 2011, with its World War II setting, it seemed like Marvel Studios very well could’ve continued to feature flashbacks to the war in Cap sequels that might’ve given us other heroes of that era, possibly including the Invaders. But it never happened, and with Namor’s rights apparently tied up in legal limbo back then, a live-action Invaders just wasn’t in the cards. (Though the general idea of the Invaders was mashed up with the Howling Commandos around the time of The First Avenger, but that’s just not the same thing.)

But Namor’s rights were eventually resolved, as he finally debuted in Black Panther: Wakanda Forever with Tenoch Huerta playing the underwater king. Indeed, Namor will be back for Avengers: Doomsday, and now we also know that the original android Human Torch existed during the war years as well. Since Namor is a mutant who is apparently centuries old, it is conceivable that he left the kingdom of Talokan during World War II and wound up fighting alongside Captain America, Bucky, and the Torch. Heck, maybe there was even a Toro back then!

Did VisionQuest just give Marvel an in to tell a whole new series of MCU stories set in the World War II era and featuring the Invaders? Sure, it’s hard to picture, say, Chris Evans coming back after walking away from Marvel… or is it? Either way, just knowing that there could be a version of MCU history where Cap, the Torch, and Namor were busting Nazi skulls is good enough for me.

Talk to Scott Collura @scottcollura.bsky.social , or listen to his Star Trek podcast, Transporter Room 3 . Or do both!

articles.title: I’m Excited For Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel To Be Nothing Like Skyrim
articles.summary: The Elder Scrolls is headed to the desert region of Hammerfell and I hope the world of Sentinel looks and feels nothing like Skyrim.
articles.body:
This is an opinion piece from writer Tim Brinkhof. IGN's opinion columns represent the personal viewpoints of the writer, drawing on their own experiences and research to explore the exciting world of video games.

It feels strange to say after so long, but it’s an exciting time to be an Elder Scrolls fan. Confirming news leaked – of all places – in a news report from The Verge about AI-related layoffs at parent company Microsoft, developer Bethesda has not only given us a title for The Elder Scrolls 6, Sentinel, but also a quote, one that suggests the story will have something to do with time travel.

“The scroll offered only a shimmer, a veil thinly lifted to my eyes,” it says. “A future lost. A victory undone. Sands of time scattered by fate.” The quote is attributed to Yazar, Moth Priest of High Queen Iradne of Hammerfell, and dated 4E 206. It reveals two things: first, that Sentinel takes place half a decade after the events of Skyrim, and second, that Hammerfell is our next destination, the region of Tamriel home to the titular Sentinel city. And it’s that region that gives me the most to look forward to.

Though Skyrim will always have a special place in my heart, its very typical medieval fantasy aesthetic and culture saw The Elder Scrolls stray from its eccentric and otherworldly roots. A game set in Hammerfell, Skyrim’s complete opposite in climate and much else, could turn out to be the return to those roots that I have craved for over a decade. But can the developers deliver, or will they simply replace snow with sand?

Before I get into it, let me make it clear: I do not dislike Skyrim. I loved the game when it came out in 2011, and still have a lot of love for it today. I love the game’s atmosphere, and still listen to Jeremy Soule’s ethereal soundtrack – it’s often the music that lulls me to sleep. I love the designs of cities like Solitude and Markarth, and share in the popular opinion that Ulfric, Cicero, and Paarthurnax are among some of the most interesting and iconic characters that Bethesda has ever created.

One thing I don’t love as much as I did back when the game was released is how much its world reminds me of other popular fantasy franchises like The Lord of the Rings and especially Game of Thrones, which started airing just a few months before Skyrim arrived. Compared to Oblivion and Morrowind, Skyrim feels if not uninspired, then at least a little too familiar. Whiterun, as many have noted, is basically Edoras, while Ulfric’s battle for northern independence may well have been inspired by Robb Stark’s own struggles as King in the North in George R.R. Martin’s original novels.

While Bethesda isn’t to blame for this (at least, and I’ll get to this shortly, not entirely), the game’s unfavorable comparison to Oblivion and Morrowind still stands. I played both these predecessors only after completing Skyrim and didn’t expect to like them as much on account of their technical limitations. Instead, I ended up liking them more, partly because of their stranger, less familiar settings.

Where Skyrim’s Skyrim is inspired by the classic fantasy template of medieval Europe – particularly Viking Scandinavia – Oblivion’s Cyrodiil takes after ancient Rome, a time period and region that’s less frequently mined by high fantasy. The resemblance is also far less on the nose than in Skyrim, ensuring Cyrodill feels distinctly like its own place. The world is rendered even more fantastical thanks to invading Daedric forces, with large chunks of the game taking place in the hellish Deadlands, home to Mehrunes Dagon.

Morrowind goes even harder, presenting a setting that’s almost completely devoid of recognizable real-world counterparts. The province’s silt striders and building-sized fungi make Skyrim look like an American suburb in comparison, and places like Vivec City, with its grid of interconnected pyramids and giant meteor hovering above, to me have always represented the series at its wildest and most creative.

While Skyrim definitely has moments that evoke a similar emotion – I’m thinking, for example, of when you descend down the Dwemer ruins of Blackreach or visit the Daedric realm of Apocrypha in the Dragonborn DLC – I don’t think I’m stepping out of line when I say that the game as a whole offers a much more conventional and archetypical take on the fantasy genre than either of its immediate predecessors.

Whether Sentinel is going to turn things around remains to be seen. On the one hand, Hammerfell provides the perfect stage for Bethesda to do just that. Its searing deserts and tropical jungles are as far from Skyrim’s landscape as you can get, and have not been seen in the mainline series since their procedurally-generated appearance in the second Elder Scrolls game, Daggerfall (you can, of course, visit more modern renditions in The Elder Scrolls Online). On top of this, Hammerfell’s Redguards are distinctly non-Western, combining Middle Eastern, African, and Japanese influences into something not just unique to Tamriel, but fantasy in general.

On the other hand, we shouldn’t forget that Skyrim’s tameness was a deliberate design decision – one former lore master Kurt Kuhlmann has attributed not only to Todd Howard's personal preferences, but also to commercial reasons .

"If you're in charge of spending all this money and you want your studio to continue to exist and pay salaries for people, you have to make a successful commercial product," Kuhlmann told Reece "Kiwi Talkz" Reilly on YouTube , noting that Todd Howard "gravitates not towards the weird stuff."

To appeal to a larger audience, Bethesda not only streamlined combat and reduced player agency, but made sure its setting would be recognizable and inviting to casual gamers whose experience with fantasy didn’t extend beyond Tolkien’s Lord of the Rings books and Peter Jackson’s film adaptations, which were "wildly popular" at the time, according to both Kohlmann and literally anyone who was alive at the time.

This decision may have come at the cost of the franchise’s originality, but that was a price Bethesda was willing to pay. And chances are, it doesn’t regret it. Skyrim became the company’s most successful game up to that point, not to mention one of the most successful games, period. Financially speaking, we really shouldn’t expect the developers to alter the game’s winning formula – especially not after such a long and costly development cycle. And, of course, Bethesda parent company Xbox is in desperate need of a huge success, doubly so if it deems Sentinel should be an Xbox exclusive .

The title announcement should perhaps confirm that things will be much more fantastical – Sentinel itself is, afterall, very clearly a blend of North African and Middle Eastern architecture and culture, and the sand-swept teaser only hammer(fell)s home the locale’s unique climate. But there’s reason to be skeptical. Look at a map, and you’ll see the city of Sentinel sits on the shores of the Iliac Bay, across from another province that has long been rumored (though not yet confirmed) to be a part of the game’s setting: High Rock. This second province, home to the city of Daggerfall, has a lot in common with Skyrim, both culturally and geographically. It’s more European. More British. More GRRM. More Tolkien-ish. I could easily see Bethesda leaning into those similarities to tug on people’s nostalgia strings, rather than concentrating on Sentinel, Hammerfell, and what makes that region unique and different. The title doesn’t have to dictate where we spend most of our time – Oblivion is just one small part of Oblivion, afterall.

My ideal vision for Sentinel, one I continue to hope for, is one where Bethesda uses the similarity between High Rock and Skyrim to further build up the contrast with Hammerfell. Imagine leaving Skyrim for the neighboring High Rock as Soule’s old music plays, then taking a boat across the Iliac Bay and emerging in what feels like a completely different universe, utterly and blissfully unsure what the future has in store.

I didn’t wait 15 years for more Skyrim. And so I hope that Sentinel is nothing like Skyrim.

Tim Brinkhof is a freelance writer specializing in art and history. After studying journalism at NYU, he has gone on to write for Vox, Vulture, Slate, Polygon, GQ, Esquire and more.

articles.title: Rockstar Games Releases 39 New GTA 6 Screenshots to Celebrate Two Weeks from Launch
articles.summary: Rockstar Games has released a few dozen new screenshots from GTA 6 to celebrate the game being two weeks away from launch.
articles.body:
Rockstar Games has released a few dozen new screenshots from GTA 6 to celebrate the game being two weeks away from launch.

After 13 years of waiting, GTA 6 is finally almost here. The game is exactly 14 days away from release in the United States, and fans are eager to be able to visit Vice City once again. To help make the wait a bit more bearable, Rockstar has dropped 39 new screenshots from the game, which give us new looks at Vice City, the people within it, strip clubs, and some of the rip-roaring crimes that Jason and Lucia will take part in.

Rockstar Games released what is expected to be the final trailer for GTA 6 last month , which has been airing on TV constantly since its debut online. The game's marketing is also hard to ignore, as cities around the world have been covered in billboards, posters, and bus decals. Rockstar has gone all-out in the city of Miami by taking over the Miami Heat arena with GTA branding , selling in-universe beers from the games at bars, and flying a Vice City blimp around the city. Rockstar has essentially turned Miami into Vice City in real life , flexing the game's cultural power.

On November 18, Rockstar will also host a special event it calls "A Night in Vice City," which will feature a special NBA game between the Miami Heat and the Milwaukee Bucks. The Heat will be turned into the Vice City Heat and sport GTA-themed jerseys, while also playing on a new court. It's unclear if there will be other events in the city, but it wouldn't be surprising. Miami's nightclubs have also been turned into the GTA clubs over the last couple of weeks, showing a total takeover from Rockstar.

GTA 6 will release on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Pre-loading will begin on November 10 and will take up 212 GBs of space on your storage device. The game has already racked up an estimated $750 million in pre-orders , suggesting it will break an absurd amount of records once the floodgates open on release weekend.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: GOG Announces Road Rash Touch Up and a Publishing Arm for 'New Games With a Classic Soul'
articles.summary: GOG is old enough to drink in the UK. To celebrate that milestone, the DRM-free storefront — which lets players do what they want to games once they own them, including sending them to other PCs, backing them up to hard drives, and even burning them onto discs to add to a physical collection — has announced a range of surprises.
articles.body:
GOG is old enough to drink in the UK. To celebrate that milestone, the DRM-free storefront — which lets players do what they want to games once they own them, including sending them to other PCs, backing them up to hard drives, and even burning them onto discs to add to a physical collection — has announced a range of surprises.

The company is currently on a mission to keep games available to play even after the seasons end and servers close down. Its GOG Patrons initiative has saved 300 old games, funding them to be made compatible with modern operating systems. Over 10,000 patrons have signed up to help. The latest game to benefit from this was Nox, the action RPG developed and published by Westwood Studios and EA back in 2000.

“We dig deep into the code, fixing long-lasting bugs, adjusting screen resolutions, adding controller support, missing cutscenes and much, much more,” said Marcin Paczynski, senior business development manager.

GOG has made over 1,700 fixes to old games in its preservation program. Next up, there’s good news for classic space sim and Mark Hamill fans.

The Wing Commander series — Wing Commander 1-4 games, Prophecy Gold, and Privateer 2 — is getting an anniversary edition update. GOG collaborated with modders for Prophecy, with a goal of making the game more approachable, adding controller support to offer a new way to play.

Each of these games comes with the legacy version and the touched up Anniversary Edition. For people who already own the original games on GOG, the Anniversary Editions are free to download at launch.

Ahead of those updated space sims, there’s something new on GOG right now: Road Rash. The violent motorbike racing classic got the same treatment as Wing Commander, making it compatible with modern systems and control inputs.

GOG also announced Retro Vibe, a publishing arm focused on “new games with a classic soul.” Retro Vibe releases include a VHS-fuzzed FPS with Max Payne-esque bullet time called Cop Bastard, a side-scrolling shooter with tough boss battles called The Looter, tactical cyberpunk RPG Shardpunk 2, boomer shooter with massive boomsticks Project Warlock: Lost Chapters, and the mysterious greyscale indie game After Hell Freezes Over.

You can Wishlist the full lineup of games and check them out in more detail on GOG.com . It’s a site GOG is hoping you’ll spend more time on anyway, as the service is also introducing GOG Social, a new gaming forum integrated with your game library, allowing you to tag games in posts, taking readers directly to the store page. The forum has marked spoilers, threaded replies, reactions, post edits, media support, bookmarks, topic subscriptions, and more.

Lastly, GOG Galaxy — GOG’s launcher that lets you combine your entire library from different stores into one space — is also coming to Linux. It’s landing with new customization and personalization options. Watch the entire showcase on the GOG YouTube channel .

Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

articles.title: ‘This is not a Playstation game’ – Jaissle on his Newcastle side’s struggles
articles.summary: Matthias Jaissle has urged his Newcastle players to take greater responsibility for their decision-making on the pitch, insisting they cannot be coached thro...
articles.body:
Matthias Jaissle has urged his Newcastle players to take greater responsibility for their decision-making on the pitch, insisting they cannot be coached through every moment of a game.

The Newcastle United head coach made clear on Monday following his side's loss to Everton that his players had not enacted the game plan properly .

And speaking ahead of his side's game against, Fulham, Jaissle said: "We already adjusted here and there our framework, our principles, always according to the opposition. We can support the players with that.

"In the end they are on the pitch, it's not a PlayStation game."

The German admitted that the choices made by his players recently have not been good enough, but admits that when confidence is not there, it becomes more difficult.

He emphasised that this has been spoken about within his squad, saying that they have been "encouraged" by he and his coaching staff to make better decisions.

"It's on us to build that [confidence] again", Jaissle said.

The Magpies travel to London on Saturday to face a Fulham side who are slowly beginning to improve after a poor start.

Farore's Wind is an item and spell in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. Check out IGN's guide on Farore's Wind below:

Farore's Wind is a boon gifted to Link by the Great Fairy in Zora Fountain. Upon giving Ruto's Letter to King Zora and gaining access to the Fountain, head toward the south side of the zone, where you will see a large cave opening. Head inside to find the Great Fairy Fountain.
